title: An Image is Worth One Word: Personalizing Text-to-Image Generation using Textual Inversion
layout_note: An L-shaped path: the quoted prompt enters a tall grey Text Encoder container on the left and falls top-to-bottom through Tokenizer, token ids, Embedding Lookup, embedding vectors and Text Transformer; c_theta(y) then runs right along the bottom into a tall green Generator column, which is paired row-by-row with a grey Noised Sample column fed from the Input Sample photo at the top right. A blue rounded zoom bubble, attached to the Embedding Lookup box by two thin blue lines, enlarges the embedding table.
grouping: A large light-grey rounded container labelled Text Encoder (bottom left) holds the three green/blue step boxes and also wraps the blue zoom bubble; the generator outputs sit in a separate light-green rounded column labelled Generator, the noised targets in a light-grey rounded column labelled Noised Sample; the prompt and the input photo each sit in a cream rounded box at the top.
shapes_depth: Flat rounded rectangles with thin outlines, no shadows: pale green for Tokenizer and Text Transformer, pale blue for Embedding Lookup. Token ids and embeddings are bare text/math under thick black arrows. The embedding table is drawn as rows of four coloured cells (yellow, peach, purple, green) labelled v_0, v_73, v_508, v_701; the new embedding v_* is a separate green-labelled row of four cells each holding '?'. Small black padlock icons mark the frozen table, Text Transformer and Generator.
proposed_highlight: The one thing being learned, the pseudo-word embedding v_*, is set apart below the embedding table as its own row of '?' cells inside the zoom bubble, while every other component carries a padlock; the placeholder S_* also appears in the quoted prompt and as the token <*> through every step.
lesson: To show that only one tiny parameter is trained in an otherwise frozen pipeline, put a padlock on every frozen box and give the trainable vector its own row of '?' cells inside a zoom bubble, so the reader sees exactly which numbers change.
notes: year = arXiv preprint year (2208.01618); venue remembered as ICLR 2023 (not printed on the arXiv first page). The crop holds several embedded photos (generator outputs, noised samples, input sample), recorded by refs crop.

arrangement.units: One composition with three rounded sub-containers: a grey Text Encoder (left, holding the step boxes and the blue zoom bubble), a green Generator column and a grey Noised Sample column (right), plus cream boxes for the prompt and input photo at the top.
arrangement.inputs_as: a quoted prompt 'A photo of S_*' in a cream box at the top left, and a real photo labelled Input Sample in a cream box at the top right
arrangement.losses_at: not written as a loss: dashed double-headed arrows between each generator output and the matching noised sample, row by row between the two right-hand columns

taxonomy.task: personalizing a frozen text-to-image model with a learned pseudo-word

insights.structure: A grey Text Encoder container fills the left half with its steps stacked top-to-bottom and a blue zoom bubble beside them; the right third is two tall paired columns (green Generator outputs, grey Noised Samples) of four photos each.
insights.data: Tokens are drawn as their actual integer ids (508, 701, 73, <*>), embeddings as rows of coloured cells, and images as real photos of one alarm clock at four noise levels.
insights.emphasis: Padlocks on the table, Text Transformer and Generator make the single unlocked row v_* with '?' cells the obvious trainable part.
insights.flow: Thick black vertical arrows carry the prompt down through the encoder, one thick horizontal arrow labelled c_theta(y) runs along the bottom to the generator, and dashed horizontal double arrows tie each output to its noised target.
insights.avoid: The objective is implied only by unlabelled dashed double arrows, and the Generator column's photos are not explained as denoising steps, so a reader must infer the reconstruction loss from the caption.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
